en: The world's largest flower, Rafflesia arnoldii, can grow up to 1 meter in diameter and weigh as much as 11 kilograms.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth, reaching diving speeds of over 320 kilometers per hour when hunting prey.
The human body contains about 25 trillion red blood cells that continuously travel through 96,000 kilometers of blood vessels.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef ecosystem, stretching over 2,300 kilometers along the northeast coast of Australia.
The heart of a blue whale is about the size of a small car and beats only eight to ten times per minute.
Periodical cicadas spend either 13 or 17 years underground as nymphs before emerging as adults to mate and lay eggs.
A human baby is born with about 270 bones, but adults only have 206 because many bones fuse together during growth.
A single orchid seed pod can contain up to four million tiny seeds, which are so small they look like dust.
The Arctic tern migrates up to 70,000 kilometers annually between its Arctic breeding grounds and the Antarctic coast.
The average human blinks about 15 to 20 times per minute, which equals roughly 28,000 times per day.
A single leafcutter ant colony can contain up to eight million individual ants living in underground nests covering 30 square meters.
A fully grown saguaro cactus can absorb and store up to 750 liters of water during a rainstorm to survive long droughts.
